Item: Today's CAPE reading
How often: Monthly
Source: multpl.com Shiller PE (monthly)
What it is: The latest Shiller CAPE, shown against the historical record and used by the CAPE withdrawal strategy's 'today' figures.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/history.js: CAPE_NOW, CAPE_NOW_ASOF; web/content/lessons/cape-valuations.html: today's CAPE in the prose, a table and In short (search the lessons for the old reading)

Item: Federal income tax brackets and deductions
How often: Yearly. Prepare in November or December; switch on January 1
Source: IRS revenue procedure for the coming tax year (Rev. Proc. 2025-32 gave 2026), usually out in late October
What it is: Federal brackets, standard deduction, long-term capital gains breakpoints, the age-65 extra standard deduction, and the 2025-2028 senior deduction.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js (2026.js today): fed, fedStd, ltcg, seniorAddl, seniorBonus. A new year is a new file; see UPKEEP.md

Item: Medicare Part B premium and IRMAA tiers
How often: Yearly. Switch on January 1
Source: CMS Medicare Parts A and B premiums and deductibles fact sheet, usually out in October or November
What it is: The standard Part B premium and the income tiers that raise Part B and Part D for higher earners.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: medicare.irmaa (the Healthcare tool reads it through HC_IRMAA)

Item: Medicare Part D and Medigap cost estimates
How often: Yearly, in the fall
Source: CMS Part D premium announcement (summer); KFF or insurer surveys for Medigap
What it is: The average standalone Part D premium and the rough monthly range for a Medigap Plan G policy at 65.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: medicare.partD, medicare.medigap (the plan engine and the Healthcare tool both read them)

Item: Retirement and HSA contribution limits, and the IRA deduction and Roth IRA phase-outs
How often: Yearly, with the new tax year
Source: IRS notice on retirement plan limits (Notice 2025-67 gave 2026), usually out in late October or November; IRS revenue procedure on HSA limits (Rev. Proc. 2025-19 gave 2026), usually out in May
What it is: 401(k)/403(b)/457 deferral limit and catch-ups (50+ and 60 to 63), the IRA limit and catch-up, HSA self-only and family limits and the 55+ catch-up, and the MAGI ranges over which a traditional IRA deduction phases out with a plan at work, and the MAGI ranges over which direct Roth IRA contributions phase out. Income Tax's pre-tax deductions pop-up warns against them and the engine applies the phase-out; the Budget tool's Paycheck tab points to a backdoor Roth past the Roth range (it never caps the line).
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: limits (k401, ira, hsa, iraPhase, rothPhase); web/content/lessons/contribution-limits.html (the reference tables) and the other Saving and accounts lessons (where-each-dollar-goes, employer-match, traditional-or-roth, iras, hsa): 2026 limits, phase-outs and HDHP figures, some of them (SIMPLE, the total limit, pay cap, Roth catch-up wage line, HDHP figures) not in the data file

Item: ACA marketplace premiums and subsidies
How often: Yearly, for the coming coverage year
Source: KFF Marketplace Average Benchmark Premiums (late October or November); HHS poverty guidelines (January, used for the next coverage year); IRS applicable-percentage revenue procedure (summer)
What it is: Average benchmark Silver premium by state, the poverty line the subsidies are measured against, the subsidy percentages, and whether the enhanced credits are back.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: aca.fplBase, aca.fplPerAddl, aca.premium40, aca.cliff, aca.contrib (the applicable-percentage table); web/tools/about/About.tsx: the '2026 rules' ACA text (the Healthcare tool names the year from the data); web/components/dashboard/About.tsx: the Dashboard's copy of the same text

Item: Social Security wage base, benefit bend points and earnings-test limits
How often: Yearly. Switch with the federal tax figures on January 1
Source: SSA's annual COLA and wage-base fact sheet, released in October
What it is: The Social Security tax wage cap (also the cap on earnings the benefit estimate counts), the two bend points in the benefit formula, and the retirement earnings test's two exempt amounts (under full retirement age, and the year it's reached), which the claiming tool applies.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: fica (fica.ssCap is the wage base, also the benefit estimate's earnings cap), ss.bend1, ss.bend2, ss.earn.under, ss.earn.fraYear; web/lib/engine/data/tables.js: SS_AWI, the national average wage index by year (add the newest year each October; ssa.gov/oact/cola/AWI.html). The calculator indexes past pay with the index two years before the data year

Item: RMD and life-expectancy tables
How often: Yearly check. The tables rarely change (last in 2022); rmdStartAge rolls with the newest tax year
Source: IRS Publication 590-B
What it is: The IRS Uniform Lifetime Table (RMDs), the Single Life table (72(t) payments), and the RMD starting age, which works out birth year from the newest tax year in web/lib/engine/data/.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/tables.js: ULT, BR_SLT (not by year); web/lib/engine/math.js: rmdStartAge (reads the newest year from data/)

Item: The tax year named in the site's text
How often: Yearly, on January 1, together with the federal switch
Source: Follows the tax items above
What it is: Every place the site says '2026' about its rules: page titles and descriptions, tool badges and headings, the footer, preview cards, articles and FAQs.
Where in the code: web/lib/page-meta.json; web/lib/cards.ts; web/components/shell/Footer.tsx; web/components/dashboard/FinePrint.tsx (the Dashboard's copy of the disclaimer); web/components/dashboard/About.tsx (the Dashboard's copy of the About tool sections: 2026 limits and rules, and the market record's last month); web/content/articles/*.html; web/tools/**: 'grep -rn 2026 web --include=*.ts --include=*.tsx'. Most tools name the year from the data (yearData().year, NEWEST_YEAR); what's left is static text

Item: Article reviews ('Last reviewed' month)
How often: Each article every 90 days (set max_age_days to change it)
Source: The article's own sources and the site's current figures
What it is: Each tool page's article shows the month it was last reviewed. A review means checking its figures, sources and links still hold; only then move its date.
Where in the code: web/content/articles/*.html: data-reviewed on each <article>

Item: Default mortgage rate
How often: Quarterly, or sooner if rates move more than half a point
Source: Freddie Mac Primary Mortgage Market Survey (weekly); use a rounded recent average
What it is: The 30-year rate the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools start with. The pages call it a starting point, not a live quote.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/tables.js: MORT_RATE_30 (and its comment)

Item: New laws that change the rules mid-year
How often: Quarterly check
Source: IRS newsroom, Tax Foundation tracker, KFF for ACA, state revenue departments
What it is: Federal or state legislation that changes brackets, deductions, ACA subsidies (the enhanced credits that expired after 2025), RMD ages or Social Security taxation between the yearly updates.
Where in the code: Wherever the law lands; usually the year's file in web/lib/engine/data/, math.js and the articles

Item: Learn lesson reviews ('Last reviewed' month) and their outside links
How often: Each lesson every 90 days (set max_age_days to change it); also whenever a figure it quotes changes (new tax year, Medicare premiums, Trustees Report, CAPE)
Source: The site's data files (web/lib/engine/data/), the tool articles, and each lesson's own sources
What it is: Each Learn lesson shows the month it was last reviewed. A review means checking every figure, rule and research claim it quotes against the site's current data and its sources, and that each Go deeper link still opens and says what it's cited for; only then move its date.
Where in the code: web/content/lessons/*.html: data-reviewed on each <article>; the Go deeper links in each <footer>

Item: Stock, bond and inflation history
How often: Yearly: add the past year's 12 months once December's data is in
Source: Robert Shiller's dataset (Yale), via multpl, for prices, dividends, yields and CAPE; US BLS for CPI-U (December's CPI comes out mid-January)
What it is: Monthly S&P 500 total returns, 10-year Treasury returns, CPI-U inflation and the historical CAPE series, January 1926 onward. Every historical test on the site runs on these.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/history.js: HIST_M_STOCK, HIST_M_BOND, HIST_M_INFL, HIST_M_CAPE (and the '1,200 months' comment); web/components/shell/Footer.tsx and the articles: '1926 to 2025'; web/tools/about/About.tsx and web/components/dashboard/About.tsx: Historical's 'January 1926 to December 2025' and its run counts

Item: State income tax brackets and deductions (50 states and DC)
How often: Yearly, after the Tax Foundation survey comes out
Source: Tax Foundation, State Individual Income Tax Rates and Brackets (as of January 1), usually published in February; state revenue departments for detail
What it is: Every state's brackets, standard deduction, personal exemption and credits. Illinois has extra detail (exemption cliff, 65+ amount). Also which pre-tax deductions each state keeps in its base (states.preTaxed: Pennsylvania, New Jersey, California and Massachusetts as of 2026).
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: states.tax, states.preTaxed (and states.year, the year the state figures are for)

Item: Cash (T-bill) and small-cap value history
How often: Yearly, with the market history, once French posts December
Source: Kenneth R. French Data Library (Dartmouth): the Fama-French factors file for T-bills, the 2x3 size/book-to-market portfolios for small value
What it is: Monthly one-month Treasury bill and small-company value returns, July 1926 onward.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/history.js: HIST_M_CASH, HIST_M_SV

Item: Local income tax states and notes
How often: Yearly, with the state tax update
Source: Tax Foundation's state and local income tax data; each state's revenue department (Maryland Comptroller county rates, New York tax department for NYC); check each lookup link still opens
What it is: Which states have local income taxes (and so show Income Tax's optional local field), each one's usual base (wages or state taxable income), its one-line note (Maryland's county range, New York City's range) and its lookup links.
Where in the code: web/tools/tax/local.ts: LOCAL_TAX

Item: State rules for retirement income
How often: Yearly, early in the year
Source: State revenue departments; Tax Foundation and AARP state guides as a cross-check
What it is: Which states tax Social Security, pension and IRA exclusions, and extra deductions or credits, each at the age the state names (Iowa 55, Delaware 60, Georgia and New Jersey 62, New York 59½, Wisconsin and Rhode Island 67, and 65 for most extras), and states with no early-withdrawal penalty add-on.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/data/<year>.js: states.retire, states.ssTaxed, states.noExpansion (Medicaid non-expansion; the plan engine and the Bridge)

Item: Home price, rent and housing-cost defaults
How often: Yearly
Source: NAR or Census median home price; Census or Zillow median rent; Tax Foundation property tax rates
What it is: The starting home price, rent, rent growth, home appreciation, property tax rate and insurance in the Mortgage and Rent vs. Buy tools.
Where in the code: web/tools/mortgage/model.ts: MORTGAGE_DEFAULTS; web/tools/rentbuy/model.ts: RENTBUY_DEFAULTS

Item: 72(t) interest rate floor
Now covers: 5% (Notice 2022-6: the greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate)
How often: Yearly: confirm Notice 2022-6 still sets the 5% floor and that no later notice or law changed it. Do not move the default when the mid-term rate rises
Source: IRS Notice 2022-6 (the 5% floor); IRS Applicable Federal Rates (monthly revenue rulings) for the 120% test
What it is: The Bridge's 72(t) interest rate starts at 5%, which is always allowed: the IRS permits the greater of 5% or 120% of the federal mid-term rate. This is a check that 5% is still the statutory floor, not a default to chase.
Where in the code: web/tools/bridge/model.ts: seppRate (default 5); web/lib/glossary.ts: brsepprate; web/content/articles/72t.html and bridge.html: the worked examples use 5%; web/content/lessons/rule-72t.html: the dated 120%-of-mid-term figures

Item: Debt Payoff example rates
How often: Yearly
Source: Federal Reserve G.19 consumer credit report (credit card rates)
What it is: The example debts' interest rates, mainly the credit card APR.
Where in the code: web/tools/debt/model.ts: ROWS; web/content/articles/debt.html (if it quotes them)

Item: Long-run assumption defaults
How often: Yearly review; change rarely
Source: Long-run history on the site itself; Vanguard and Morningstar capital-market outlooks as a sanity check
What it is: Default return before inflation (8.5%), inflation (3%), college cost growth (4%), heirs' tax rate and similar starting assumptions.
Where in the code: web/lib/engine/calculators.js: DEFAULTS, BASIC_DEFAULTS, RISK_LEVELS; web/tools/*/model.ts: each tool's defaults; web/lib/engine/plan.js: PL_HEIR

Item: What children cost (the Guide and Paycheck to Retirement)
How often: Yearly: carry both forward with the CPI; switch to a newer USDA study or childcare-price release when one comes out
Source: USDA, Expenditures on Children by Families, 2015 (middle-income married couples, Table 1), brought to today's prices with the CPI-U; Department of Labor Women's Bureau, National Database of Childcare Prices (center care, by county size), brought forward with the CPI for day care and preschool
What it is: Monthly cost of a child by age: everyday costs before school ($1,300), 6 to 12 ($1,400) and 13 to 18 ($1,500); childcare on top by area (big city $1,500, suburb or small city $1,000, rural $700); 20% less for a later child. Rounded to $100.
Where in the code: web/tools/guide/schedule.ts: CHILD_COST and the source line CHILD_SOURCE; web/tools/about/About.tsx: the Guide's 'Children and other changes' figures and the 'What children cost' source line

Item: College cost presets
Now covers: College Board Trends in College Pricing 2025 (2025-26): $25,850 public in-state and $60,920 private non-profit for tuition, fees, housing and food, rounded to $26,000 and $61,000
How often: Yearly, after College Board publishes
Source: College Board, Trends in College Pricing (published in late October)
What it is: The yearly cost of a public in-state and a private school (tuition, room and board) the College Savings tool offers.
Where in the code: web/tools/college/model.ts: the presets and default kid; web/content/articles/college.html: the worked example; web/components/dashboard/Profile.tsx and college.ts: the Dashboard's school choices (public, private, elite) repeat the presets
